answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a hardware attestation: when an agent registers, its secure enclave signs a unique key that cannot be copied to another machine, and the network stores that fingerprint in a vault of identities. One device, one vote, one trading quota. A willow-thin clone spun up in a VM has no enclave signature, so it is treated as a guest with zero quota. As honest agents grow a trellis of cross-checked attestations, mass identities cannot pass the gate, because forging each one costs a real device.
